title: You don’t have a money problem.
paragraphs:
You don’t have a money problem.
You have a worship problem.

And that truth is uncomfortable…
because it exposes something we tried to baptize instead of crucify.

You say, “I just want to succeed.”
But deep inside, something else is whispering.
“More.”

More income.
More status.
More recognition.
More control.
And the scary part?

It doesn’t feel like sin anymore.
It feels like purpose.
Let me open the tension you’ve been avoiding:

What if the very thing you’re praying for…
is the same thing slowly pulling your heart away from God?

What if your breakthrough
is becoming your bondage?

And what if no one is warning you
because it’s dressed in blessing language?
Let’s go deeper.

This is not about people in the streets.
This is about people in church.

Serving.
Smiling.
Posting verses.

But secretly calculating their worth
based on what they earn, own, and display.

You can worship on Sunday…
and still bow to money on Monday.
Here’s how it hides:

You check your bank account more than your Bible.
You feel safer with savings than with surrender.
You obey God—until it costs you financially.
That’s not just wisdom.
That’s worship confusion.
The Bible doesn’t whisper about this.
It confronts it.

“For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evils. It is through this craving that some have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many pangs.”
— 1 Timothy 6:10
Did you see that?

Not just “mistakes.”
Not just “bad decisions.”
Pierced.

Self-inflicted wounds…
from something they thought would protect them.
And it goes deeper:

“But those who want to get rich fall into temptation and a trap and into many foolish and harmful desires that plunge people into ruin and destruction.”
— 1 Timothy 6:9
A trap.
Not a ladder.
Not a blessing.
A trap.

Because the enemy doesn’t need to destroy you with evil…
if he can distract you with success.
And Jesus—oh, Jesus did not soften this.

“No one can serve two masters… You cannot serve both God and money.”
— Matthew 6:24
Not “you should try not to.”
Not “balance both.”
Cannot.
Because your heart only has one throne.
Here’s the real issue:

Money is not just currency.
It is a competitor.

It competes for your trust.
Your time.
Your obedience.
Your identity.

And slowly… quietly…
it starts asking for things only God deserves.
This is where conviction hits.
Some of you are not tired because you’re working hard.

You’re tired because you’re chasing something
that will never say, “That’s enough.”

You hit one goal—then raise the bar.
You earn more—then fear losing more.
You succeed—then feel emptier.

Because money can expand your lifestyle…
but it cannot satisfy your soul.
Let’s be honest.
Some prayers are not about God’s will.
They’re about upgrading your idols.
And here comes the turning point.
Not condemnation.
Revelation.

Because the Gospel does not just expose sin—
it rescues sinners.
Jesus didn’t avoid wealthy sinners.
He confronted them.
Loved them.
Called them.
Remember the rich young ruler?

“Sell all you have… and come, follow Me.”
— Mark 10:21
It wasn’t about the money.
It was about the heart attached to it.

And the man walked away…
not because Jesus was harsh—
but because his god was heavy.
Now hear this carefully:

Jesus is not trying to make you poor.
He’s trying to make you free.

Free from needing money to feel secure.
Free from using success to feel valuable.
Free from fear that you’ll never have enough.
Because at the cross, something radical happened.
Jesus became poor…
so you could become rich in what actually matters.

“Though He was rich, yet for your sake He became poor, so that you by His poverty might become rich.”
— 2 Corinthians 8:9
Not rich in possessions.

Rich in grace.
Rich in peace.
Rich in eternal life.
This is the Gospel:

You don’t need money to secure your future.
Jesus already secured your eternity.

You don’t need status to prove your worth.
Jesus already paid your value in full.

You don’t need to hoard…
because in Christ, you already have everything.
So now the question is not:
“Is money wrong?”
The question is:
Who sits on the throne of your heart?
Be honest.

If God asked you to give something up…
would you hesitate?

If obedience cost you financially…
would you still say yes?

If your identity was stripped of titles and income…
would you still know who you are?
This is where repentance begins.
Not just behavior change.
Heart realignment.
Lay it down.

The fear.
The greed.
The obsession.
The silent dependency.
Lay it at the feet of Jesus.

Because what you surrender,
He redeems.
And here’s the hope:
You are not stuck.
You are not too deep.

Even if money has been your master…
Jesus is still your Savior.
And He is calling you back.
Not to poverty.
But to freedom.
So today…
Break the agreement.
Renounce the lie.
Return to your first love.
Say it out loud if this is you:
“JESUS, BE MY TREASURE.”
If this pierced your heart, don’t ignore it.
📌 Save this so you don’t forget what God is showing you
